newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile judge grills Davila and two brokers.
newsitem.headline: Chile judge grills Davila and two brokers.

text.p: A Chilean judge quizzed Thursday former Codelco futures operator Juan Pablo Davila face- to-face with representatives of two foreign brokers as part of his probe into loss-making futures deals uncovered in 1994.
Judge Jose Benquis was trying to throw light on Davila's claims that futures trades profits were used by Codelco to buy a scanner for a military hospital in the late 1980s, said judicial sources.

The issue is sensitive as the alleged deal occured in the last years of General Augusto Pinochet's military government. The magistrate questioned Davila together with Rene Riveros, from brokers Charles Pixley and Andres Vorwerck, representative for Metallgesellschaft METG.Fu about the allegations which Codelco has denied.
Davila said Codelco bought the scanner using funds from deals involving 100,000 tonnes of copper from the corporation's Andina division which were handled by Metallgesellschaft.

Codelco started a law suit last year in London against the German brokers accusing them of paying huge secret commissions to Davila. The corporation has issued a similar writ against Belgian traders Sogemin Limited. Both companies have denied any wrongdoing.

Davila, once Codelco's top futures trader, was fired as soon as the scandal broke in early 1994. The ex-dealer has been charged with fraud and carrying out business "incompatible" with his position in Codelco.
